kf: A **blue naevus** is a benign collection of **dermal melanocytes**: a steel-blue, firm, dome-shaped papule.
Blue because deep pigment scatters back blue light (**Tyndall effect**).
Head and neck, backs of hands and feet, buttocks; usually under 1 cm.
Reassure if long-standing and stable; dermoscopy shows homogeneous blue pigment.
Refer new, enlarging or large (>1 cm) lesions in adults: nodular or metastatic melanoma can look blue.
myths: **"Blue moles are bruises or tattoos"**: a persisting blue papule without trauma is often a blue naevus, but must be stable.
patho_lead: Melanocytes that **stopped in the dermis** during development produce pigment deep in the skin.

mech.t: Melanocytes travelling from the neural crest to the epidermis stop in the dermis.
A mutation drives a small clonal proliferation.
Deep pigment scatters blue light back to the eye.
mech.cap: Deep dermal pigment looks blue (Tyndall effect); superficial pigment looks brown.

histo: Dendritic, heavily pigmented melanocytes and melanophages in the dermis; cellular blue naevus has nodules of spindle cells.
comp: Rarely, malignant blue naevus (melanoma arising in a blue naevus).
prog: Stable for life in almost all.
